readingHtml:
The Science of Memory

How does your brain remember?

A.Have you ever wondered how you remember your best friend's face, but forget where you put your phone? The human brain is the most complex machine in the known universe. It contains about 86 billion neurons (nerve cells). These neurons connect with each other to form a huge network.

B.When you learn something new, your brain processes the information. For example, if you memorize a new English word, the neurons send electrical signals to each other. Over time, this connection becomes stronger. The brain then stores this word in your memory. But memories are not always accurate. Sometimes, a specific smell or sound can trigger a memory you thought you had lost.

C.Scientists have discovered that sleep is very important. While you are sleeping, your brain organizes information. It decides what to keep and what to forget. So, if you want to recall what you studied yesterday, make sure you get enough sleep! Learning is a skill, and your brain is the ultimate tool.
